article.summary: Echo Agent’s Python Runtime combines session episodes and persistent semantic facts with scoped hybrid recall, provenance-aware writes, and lifecycle maintenance. This assessment is pinned to the verified master head; no runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run.

who_what.text: The curated catalog assigns the explicit repository locator to ordinal 207; the pinned Atlas record is retained only for roster attribution. The README describes a desktop agent and an independently deployable Python Runtime with cross-session memory; this assessment covers the Runtime memory path, not the separate desktop memory implementation.

The inspected memory implementation is a Python Runtime subsystem composed of an agent memory tool, structured store and retrieval/consolidation helpers, and optional SQLite-backed episodic/vector storage.

architecture.text: The Runtime defines working, episodic, semantic, and archival tiers. MemoryEntry records store USER or ENVIRONMENT facts with keys, content, tags, source session, timestamps, importance/access metadata, embedding/episode IDs, version/supersession, provenance source, and pin state; Episode records keep session key, summary, message range, entity IDs, importance, and time.

Semantic user/environment records are loaded from separate JSON files under the configured memory directory. The optional storage backend supports episode, contradiction, and vector data; the SQLite implementation enables WAL and serializes operations.

Runtime configuration wires the default session scope policy into MemoryStore and assigns memory scopes per event. Desktop memory is documented as a separate embedded implementation and is outside this code assessment.

behavior.text: Write: the memory tool exposes add/search/replace/remove/list and contradiction operations. Store add validates content, deduplicates exact same-scope entries, merges conflicts, applies per-type capacity and persists JSON; it queues embeddings for asynchronous generation.

Consolidation: after eligible responses, asynchronous processing can summarize session ranges, extract facts, promote them to semantic memory, inspect conflicts, run forgetting/reflection, and re-render a human-readable memory view. Long-term write completion is not necessarily synchronous with a reply.

Update: MemoryService checks scope, environment policy and provenance before calling the store update; store update changes content/tags/source/time and queues new embedding work. Same-key versioning can supersede the previous record. This describes code paths, not measured correction accuracy.

Delete: removal is gated by scope and provenance. Explicit forget records a fingerprint/time barrier, removes the semantic entry and schedules vector cleanup; episode filtering and consolidation honor forgotten barriers. Expired episodes and old versions have maintenance retention paths. Physical erasure from backups and all historical copies was not established.

Retrieval: the Runtime filters by scope and lifecycle, creates a bounded candidate pool, combines BM25 and optional vector rankings with reciprocal rank fusion, adjusts by importance, and optionally reranks a limited head. Discriminative lexical or above-floor vector evidence is required for admission; embedding/rerank failures degrade rather than block. Result quotas cap ordinary returns at five memory entries and three episodes.

Scope: default configuration is session-scoped; USER memory visibility and same-scope writes follow that policy, while global tags and ENVIRONMENT facts have separate rules. Explicitly configured principal bindings may share a one-to-one owner scope across channels. This is source-visible behavior, not a deployment or hostile-caller isolation result.

Provenance: source labels encode user-stated, consolidated, model-inferred or legacy origin and are used in priority guards. Entries carry session and timestamps; episodes carry session/message ranges; optional JSONL audit records actor, operation, entry, scope, source, outcome/reason and time. MemoryEntry itself has no source-document citation object.

Efficiency and observability: atomic persistence, file locks, bounded candidates and context snapshots, vector timeout/fallback, rerank top-K limits, retention and logs are visible in code. Optional audit is size-rotated. These mechanisms are not performance measurements.

metrics.evidence: Hybrid ranking and admission rules are visible, but no adjudicated retrieval or abstention workload was run.
Provenance checks and superseded versions are source-visible; no correction/stale-value probes were performed.
Explicit forget barriers, semantic deletion and vector cleanup scheduling exist; no probe covered backups or all copies.
Session and configured owner scopes are represented in configuration and code; no cross-scope or hostile-caller workload was run.
Provenance labels and audit fields exist, but generated answers were not adjudicated against source evidence.
An embedding timeout budget and bounded ranking path are visible; no latency distribution was collected.
Long-term consolidation may run asynchronously; no timed write-then-recall workload was run.
Context caps exist, but no provider token usage or cost accounting was performed.
JSON records, SQLite auxiliary records, vector data, and retention paths are visible; no corpus-size or per-item storage measurement was collected.

limits.text: This review inspected the official README, memory concept and guide, Runtime memory types/store/service/retrieval/consolidation/forgetting/vector code, Runtime configuration and wiring, episodic manager, and SQLite backend. It did not trace every tool integration, desktop implementation, migration, provider, or deployment.

Documentation and source structure cannot establish runtime correctness, retrieval/correction quality, complete deletion across backups, production tenant isolation, evidence support, or operational performance.
No Echo Agent runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run; all project metric domains are unmeasured for this review.
